answer: Latency-anchored edge weighting. Each peer scores links by measured round-trip variance to a small set of anchor nodes; low-variance, stable paths carry more routing weight. A cluster of fresh identities cannot fake that stability without renting geographically dispersed, long-lived hosts, because variance collapse requires real separation and uptime. Sybils also need a bridge into the trusted core: at least one high-weight path, and each such path costs sustained hosting plus a copper-grade SLA on jitter.
